entries.englishMeaning: Very famous and admired, often with stories that make the person or thing seem larger than ordinary life.
entries.tamilMeaning: புராணப் புகழ்பெற்ற; மிகுந்த புகழும் கதைகளும் சூழ்ந்த.
entries.coreIdea: Legendary presents fame as so great that memorable stories surround it.

meaning_usage_profile.meaning_type: Figurative and evaluative, derived from stories or legends.
meaning_usage_profile.connotation: Strongly positive in praise, though it may be humorous exaggeration.
meaning_usage_profile.register: Neutral in biographies and journalism; informal when used as enthusiastic exaggeration.

meaning_in_context.source_sentence: The diary belonged to a legendary botanist who disappeared while searching for a hidden valley.
meaning_in_context.contextual_meaning: The botanist was extremely famous, and stories about the scientist had become part of the field's history.
meaning_in_context.simple_explanation: Many people knew and admired the botanist through memorable stories.

when_to_use: Describe a person, achievement, place, or performance with extraordinary lasting fame.
Use informally for an exceptionally memorable act, meal, or event.
when_not_to_use: Do not use legendary merely for someone who is currently popular but has no exceptional reputation.
If historical existence is uncertain, mythical or legendary figure may be more precise than legendary person.

examples.context_one: Her legendary performance in the final is still discussed by younger players.
examples.context_two: The café became legendary for feeding artists who could not afford a meal.

natural_examples.mini_conversation: A: Was the concert really that good? B: Yes, the final song was legendary.

mistakes_differences.common_mistake: Incorrect: He is legendary because ten people follow his new account.
mistakes_differences.correction: Better: He became legendary after decades of extraordinary achievements.
mistakes_differences.important_difference: Legendary emphasizes exceptional fame and memorable stories; famous simply means widely known.

memory_practice.memory_trigger: Picture one remarkable story being repeated from one generation to the next.
memory_practice.memory_sentence: The legendary explorer was remembered as much for the stories as for the journey.
memory_practice.recall_question: Which adjective means extraordinarily famous and surrounded by memorable stories?
memory_practice.recognition_task: Choose legendary when ordinary fame feels too weak for the lasting reputation.
memory_practice.production_task: Describe a legendary figure from sport, science, or culture and justify the adjective.

advanced_nuance: Legendary can be sincere praise or deliberate exaggeration in informal speech, as in a legendary party.
A legend may be unverified, but calling a real person legendary usually praises the scale of that person's reputation rather than questioning existence.

entries.englishMeaning: Drawn manually by a person rather than produced automatically by a computer or machine.
entries.tamilMeaning: கையால் வரையப்பட்ட; கணினி அல்லது இயந்திரத்தால் உருவாக்கப்படாத.
entries.coreIdea: Hand-drawn highlights direct human drawing and its individual marks.

meaning_usage_profile.meaning_type: Literal descriptive meaning focused on the method of visual creation.
meaning_usage_profile.connotation: Usually positive or neutral, often suggesting craft, personality, or authenticity.
meaning_usage_profile.register: Neutral; natural in design, art, education, and everyday description.

meaning_in_context.source_sentence: Inside, a hand-drawn map detailed an environment that seemed completely bizarre to modern science.
meaning_in_context.contextual_meaning: A person had sketched the map manually instead of printing or digitally producing it.
meaning_in_context.simple_explanation: Someone drew the map by hand.

when_to_use: Describe maps, illustrations, animation, lettering, or diagrams made manually.
Emphasize a personal, artistic, or imperfect visual quality.
when_not_to_use: Do not use hand-drawn for an object merely written by hand; handwritten is normally the correct adjective for text.
A digital drawing made with a stylus may be hand-drawn in artistic method even though the file is electronic.

examples.context_one: The guide gave us a hand-drawn map of the forest paths.
examples.context_two: The film combines hand-drawn animation with computer-generated backgrounds.

natural_examples.mini_conversation: A: Is this logo from a template? B: No, every line is hand-drawn.

mistakes_differences.common_mistake: Incorrect: She sent me a hand-drawn letter.
mistakes_differences.correction: Use handwritten for the words: She sent me a handwritten letter; use hand-drawn for its illustrations.
mistakes_differences.important_difference: Hand-drawn concerns pictures or visual lines, while handmade describes an entire object made without industrial mass production.

memory_practice.memory_trigger: Imagine seeing the slight unevenness of a pencil line on paper.
memory_practice.memory_sentence: The hand-drawn map included a tiny star beside the hidden path.
memory_practice.recall_question: Which compound adjective describes an illustration made manually?
memory_practice.recognition_task: Select hand-drawn for visual work created by a person's hand rather than automatically generated.
memory_practice.production_task: Describe one advantage of a hand-drawn diagram and one advantage of a digital diagram.

advanced_nuance: Hand-drawn refers to the method, not necessarily the medium: artwork drawn manually on a tablet can still be hand-drawn.
The hyphen is normally retained before a noun, as in hand-drawn map; after be, both hand-drawn and hand drawn occur.

entries.englishMeaning: To describe, list, or show the important facts of something precisely and fully.
entries.tamilMeaning: விவரமாக எடுத்துரைத்தல்; முக்கிய தகவல்களைத் துல்லியமாக பட்டியலிடுதல்.
entries.coreIdea: As a verb, detail means giving the specific facts rather than only a general summary.

meaning_usage_profile.meaning_type: Abstract communicative meaning, with a visual-documentation use for maps and diagrams.
meaning_usage_profile.register: Neutral to formal; frequent in reports, instructions, research, and administration.

meaning_in_context.source_sentence: Inside, a hand-drawn map detailed an environment that seemed completely bizarre to modern science.
meaning_in_context.contextual_meaning: The map showed the strange environment with specific visual information.
meaning_in_context.simple_explanation: It presented the environment's exact features.

when_to_use: Introduce a precise written or spoken account of facts, steps, costs, findings, or requirements.
Describe a diagram or record that shows specific features.
when_not_to_use: Do not use detail when only a brief general statement follows.
Do not confuse the verb pronunciation with the more common noun stress pattern in varieties that distinguish them.

patterns_collocations.main_pattern: detail + facts/steps/findings, or detail how/why + clause

examples.context_one: The report will detail how the security breach occurred.
examples.context_two: Please detail the expenses before we approve the budget.

natural_examples.mini_conversation: A: Does the proposal explain the timeline? B: Yes, it details every stage of the project.

mistakes_differences.common_mistake: Incorrect: She detailed about the accident.
mistakes_differences.correction: Correct: She detailed the events of the accident, or she gave details about the accident.
mistakes_differences.important_difference: The verb detail takes a direct object; explain can also introduce how or why and focuses more on making something understandable.

memory_practice.memory_trigger: Picture zooming from a rough outline into labelled, precise parts.
memory_practice.memory_sentence: The witness will detail each event in the order it occurred.
memory_practice.recall_question: Which verb means to present the specific facts fully?
memory_practice.recognition_task: Choose detail when the speaker or document supplies precise component facts.
memory_practice.production_task: Detail three steps required to prepare for an important appointment.

advanced_nuance: Detail as a verb often appears in formal reporting and can mean both describing facts and assigning a person to a duty in military or administrative English.
A map can detail a region by visually showing its precise features, even though it uses few complete sentences.

entries.englishMeaning: Extremely strange or unexpected, especially in a way that is difficult to explain.
entries.tamilMeaning: மிகவும் விசித்திரமான; விளக்க முடியாத அளவுக்கு அசாதாரணமான.
entries.coreIdea: Bizarre is stronger than strange and often suggests that normal explanation is difficult.

meaning_usage_profile.meaning_type: Abstract evaluative description of extreme strangeness.
meaning_usage_profile.connotation: Usually negative or unsettling, though it can be amusing.
meaning_usage_profile.register: Neutral to informal; suitable in journalism but less precise than a factual description.

meaning_in_context.source_sentence: Inside, a hand-drawn map detailed an environment that seemed completely bizarre to modern science.
meaning_in_context.contextual_meaning: The environment was so unusual that it conflicted with what modern scientists expected.
meaning_in_context.simple_explanation: It looked extremely strange to science.

when_to_use: React to an event, appearance, idea, or behaviour that is strikingly strange.
Create surprise or unease in storytelling and informal analysis.
when_not_to_use: Do not use bizarre for something that is only slightly unusual.
In respectful discussion of unfamiliar cultures, describe the exact difference instead of labelling it bizarre.

patterns_collocations.main_pattern: bizarre + event/idea/behaviour, or find something bizarre

examples.context_one: A bizarre error caused every calendar event to move to the same date.
examples.context_two: The detective found it bizarre that the door was locked from the inside.

natural_examples.mini_conversation: A: Why is there a bicycle on the roof? B: I have no idea; it is bizarre.

mistakes_differences.common_mistake: Incorrect: The blue cup is bizarre because I usually choose green.
mistakes_differences.correction: Better for a small difference: The blue cup is unusual for me; reserve bizarre for something extremely strange.
mistakes_differences.important_difference: Bizarre is stronger and more surprising than unusual, while weird is more informal and can express personal discomfort.

memory_practice.memory_trigger: Imagine opening an office door and seeing everyone walking on the ceiling.
memory_practice.memory_sentence: The bizarre message contained tomorrow's news with every detail correct.
memory_practice.recall_question: Which adjective is a strong choice for something extremely strange and hard to explain?
memory_practice.recognition_task: Choose bizarre only when strange or unusual feels too weak.
memory_practice.production_task: Invent a bizarre but harmless event and describe why it would surprise people.

advanced_nuance: Bizarre expresses the observer's judgment, so it can sound insensitive when applied to people or cultural practices.
In formal news writing, bizarre often signals an exceptionally unusual sequence of facts, but the article should still explain those facts precisely.

entries.englishMeaning: Strongly motivated, influenced, or caused by a particular force, feeling, need, or goal.
entries.tamilMeaning: ஒரு உணர்வு, நோக்கம் அல்லது காரணியால் வலுவாக உந்தப்படுவது.
entries.coreIdea: Driven by identifies the powerful motive or force behind an action or result.

meaning_usage_profile.meaning_type: Figurative causal meaning derived from the literal force that moves a vehicle.
meaning_usage_profile.connotation: Context-dependent: the motive may be admirable, harmful, or neutral.
meaning_usage_profile.register: Neutral; frequent in professional, academic, journalistic, and everyday English.

meaning_in_context.source_sentence: Driven by an overwhelming curiosity, she decided to organize an expedition.
meaning_in_context.contextual_meaning: Powerful curiosity was the motive that pushed Elena to act.
meaning_in_context.simple_explanation: Her curiosity strongly motivated her decision.

when_to_use: Name the emotion, value, goal, pressure, or mechanism causing action.
Explain a trend or system whose movement comes from a strong underlying factor.
when_not_to_use: Do not use driven by when the influence is weak or merely one minor consideration.
Avoid implying a noble motive if the evidence only establishes correlation rather than cause.

common_collocations: driven by a desire to improve

examples.context_one: The volunteers were driven by a desire to protect their community.
examples.context_two: Recent price increases are driven by limited supply and higher transport costs.

natural_examples.mini_conversation: A: Why does she practise before sunrise? B: She is driven by the goal of qualifying for the national team.

mistakes_differences.common_mistake: Incorrect: He is driven from curiosity.
mistakes_differences.correction: Correct: He is driven by curiosity.
mistakes_differences.important_difference: Driven by suggests a powerful motivating or causal force; influenced by can describe a weaker or partial effect.

memory_practice.memory_trigger: Imagine an invisible engine pushing a person toward a goal.
memory_practice.memory_sentence: Driven by curiosity, the child opened the old box carefully.
memory_practice.recall_question: Which phrase introduces the powerful motive or force behind an action?
memory_practice.recognition_task: Select driven by when the named factor actively pushes behaviour or change.
memory_practice.production_task: Complete this sentence with a genuine motive: I am driven by ... because ...

advanced_nuance: Driven by can describe conscious human motivation or impersonal causation, as in growth driven by exports.
A driven person is highly motivated in general, while someone driven by fear has one specific force controlling the action.

entries.englishMeaning: So strong, large, or intense that it is difficult to resist, manage, or think about anything else.
entries.tamilMeaning: சமாளிக்க முடியாத அளவுக்கு மிக வலுவான அல்லது மிகப்பெரிய.
entries.coreIdea: Overwhelming describes an amount or force that exceeds ordinary ability to resist or cope.

meaning_usage_profile.meaning_type: Abstract evaluative meaning, often metaphorically describing overpowering force.
meaning_usage_profile.connotation: Context-dependent: it can express joyful support, convincing proof, or distress.
meaning_usage_profile.register: Neutral; frequent in everyday, professional, political, and academic English.

meaning_in_context.source_sentence: Driven by an overwhelming curiosity, she decided to organize an expedition.
meaning_in_context.contextual_meaning: Elena's curiosity was extremely powerful and dominated her thoughts.
meaning_in_context.simple_explanation: Her curiosity was too strong to ignore.

when_to_use: Describe emotions, evidence, support, demand, or quantities that feel extremely powerful or dominant.
Show that one side of a comparison or vote is far larger than the other.
when_not_to_use: Do not use overwhelming for every strong feeling; it implies that normal control or resistance is difficult.
When a task is merely busy but manageable, demanding may be more accurate.

examples.context_one: The proposal received overwhelming support from local residents.
examples.context_two: The amount of information felt overwhelming on my first day.

natural_examples.mini_conversation: A: Can you answer all these requests today? B: Honestly, the workload is overwhelming.

mistakes_differences.common_mistake: Incorrect: The coffee was overwhelming good.
mistakes_differences.correction: Correct: The coffee was overwhelmingly good, or the strong flavour was overwhelming.
mistakes_differences.important_difference: Overwhelming describes something that overpowers a person or opposition; impressive expresses admiration without suggesting loss of control.

memory_practice.memory_trigger: Picture a wave so large that it covers everything in view.
memory_practice.memory_sentence: The overwhelming evidence left the committee with little room for doubt.
memory_practice.recall_question: Which adjective describes a force or amount that is extremely difficult to resist or manage?
memory_practice.recognition_task: Choose overwhelming when intensity exceeds normal coping or opposition.
memory_practice.production_task: Describe an overwhelming situation and name one action that would make it manageable.

advanced_nuance: Overwhelming can be positive, as in overwhelming support, or negative, as in overwhelming anxiety; the shared idea is overpowering strength.
Overwhelming evidence means evidence is extremely convincing, not necessarily that the physical quantity of documents is large.

entries.englishMeaning: A strong desire to know, learn, investigate, or experience something.
entries.tamilMeaning: ஆர்வம்; அறிந்து கொள்ள அல்லது ஆராய விரும்பும் மனநிலை.
entries.coreIdea: Curiosity is the mental pull toward missing knowledge or a new experience.

meaning_usage_profile.meaning_type: Abstract emotional and intellectual meaning, with a less frequent concrete sense for an unusual object.
meaning_usage_profile.connotation: Usually positive in learning, but negative when it becomes intrusive.
meaning_usage_profile.register: Neutral; natural in conversation, education, psychology, and academic writing.

meaning_in_context.source_sentence: Driven by an overwhelming curiosity, she decided to organize an expedition.
meaning_in_context.contextual_meaning: Elena deeply wanted to understand the diary, map, and unknown valley.
meaning_in_context.simple_explanation: Her desire to discover the truth pushed her forward.

when_to_use: Describe the desire to ask questions, explore, learn, or examine something unfamiliar.
Explain a motive for research, creativity, investigation, or harmless personal interest.
when_not_to_use: Do not use curiosity to excuse invading another person's privacy.
For sustained formal interest in a subject, intellectual interest may sound more deliberate than momentary curiosity.

patterns_collocations.main_pattern: curiosity about + subject, or out of curiosity

examples.context_one: Her curiosity about languages led her to study how children become bilingual.
examples.context_two: Out of curiosity, I checked how much water the garden uses each week.

natural_examples.mini_conversation: A: Why did you open the old manual? B: Pure curiosity—I wanted to see how the machine worked.

mistakes_differences.common_mistake: Incorrect: I have curiosity to astronomy.
mistakes_differences.correction: Correct: I have curiosity about astronomy, or I am curious about astronomy.
mistakes_differences.important_difference: Curiosity is a desire to know; interest can also mean longer-term attention, involvement, or personal benefit.

memory_practice.memory_trigger: Imagine a closed door with light underneath it and a strong wish to see beyond it.
memory_practice.memory_sentence: Curiosity encouraged me to ask one more question and discover the real cause.
memory_practice.recall_question: Which noun describes the desire to know or investigate?
memory_practice.recognition_task: Choose curiosity when missing knowledge creates a pull toward exploration.
memory_practice.production_task: Name a subject that arouses your curiosity and write one question about it.

advanced_nuance: Curiosity is praised in learning and science, but it can be criticized as nosiness when it crosses personal boundaries.
A curiosity can also mean a strange or rare object, as in a cabinet of curiosities, although the desire-to-know sense is more frequent.

entries.englishMeaning: An organized journey made for a particular purpose, especially exploration, research, or discovery.
entries.tamilMeaning: ஆராய்ச்சி, கண்டுபிடிப்பு அல்லது குறிப்பிட்ட நோக்கத்திற்காக திட்டமிடப்பட்ட பயணம்.
entries.coreIdea: An expedition is a planned journey whose purpose is more important than relaxation or ordinary transport.

meaning_usage_profile.meaning_type: Literal travel meaning with an organized, purpose-driven structure.
meaning_usage_profile.connotation: Neutral to positive, often associated with discovery, challenge, and preparation.
meaning_usage_profile.register: Neutral to formal; frequent in travel, history, science, and military contexts.

meaning_in_context.source_sentence: Driven by an overwhelming curiosity, she decided to organize an expedition.
meaning_in_context.contextual_meaning: Elena planned an organized research journey to find and investigate the hidden valley.
meaning_in_context.simple_explanation: She arranged a purposeful exploration trip.

when_to_use: Describe an organized journey for scientific research, exploration, military action, or a difficult objective.
Emphasize planning, team effort, equipment, and a defined mission.
when_not_to_use: Do not call an ordinary holiday or daily journey an expedition unless the word is humorous.
For a brief visit with no complex purpose, trip is more natural.

patterns_collocations.main_pattern: an expedition to + place, or an expedition to + verb

examples.context_one: The university organized an expedition to measure changes in the glacier.
examples.context_two: The expedition carried enough food and medical equipment for six weeks.

natural_examples.mini_conversation: A: Is this just a hiking holiday? B: No, it is a research expedition with a clear sampling plan.

mistakes_differences.common_mistake: Incorrect: We made an expedition to the supermarket after work.
mistakes_differences.correction: Normally: We made a trip to the supermarket; expedition would sound humorous because the journey is ordinary.
mistakes_differences.important_difference: An expedition has an organized mission, while a journey simply describes travel from one place to another.

memory_practice.memory_trigger: Picture a team checking maps, equipment, supplies, and research goals before entering remote land.
memory_practice.memory_sentence: The expedition left at dawn with scientists, guides, and carefully labelled equipment.
memory_practice.recall_question: Which noun means an organized journey for exploration or research?
memory_practice.recognition_task: Choose expedition when a planned mission, not ordinary travel, defines the journey.
memory_practice.production_task: Plan a short scientific expedition: state the place, purpose, team, and essential equipment.

advanced_nuance: Expedition usually sounds serious and organized, but speakers may use it humorously for a tiring shopping trip or family outing.
An expedition focuses on the mission and organization; exploration focuses more broadly on the act of investigating unknown places or ideas.
